samples.summary: "falls back to the default when storage throws on read" pre-seeds memoryFormat with the default, so the assertion cannot distinguish the default fallback from the memory mirror
samples.evidence: Line 43 calls `setDateFormat(DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT)`, which sets module-level `memoryFormat = "relative"` (src/lib/date-format-preference.ts:57). The subsequent `expect(getDateFormat()).toBe(DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT)` at line 52 therefore holds whether the catch path returns `memoryFormat` or `DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` — the two values are identical here. The only thing the test genuinely proves is that `getDateFormat` does not throw; the titled behavior ("falls back to the default") is not actually distinguished. A case with `memoryFormat` unset (or set to "exact") and a throwing read would be needed to exercise the `?? DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` branch.
